story_text.value:
Plango is a Mac native security suite for anyone running AI coding tools. It works by running a custom local security model that evaluates threats against the lethal trifecta (data access, communication, exposure).

Some cool features: - Restrict Agent access by type of data (ssh keys, env files) or finder tags (finally a good reason to use the color tags in finder). - On device security model, but can switch to another local agent or bring your own key. - Review your Mac's privacy and access, apps, startup & extensions. - Automatically move env secrets into keychain. - Network blocks/allow lists, see what apps and agents are accessing. Stop them from data exfil. - Check skills and plugins for bad behavior. - Create custom rules for all of these things. - Log every action, request, block etc in an easy dashboard. - Vuln scan of all projects on your Mac.

About us: I'm Fred, long term hacker first time shower. My co-founder Rich and I care about privacy, security and believe that AI software development is the future. We have two decades of combined experience in cyber, NLP and AI and are working on this tool full time. Given how fast cyber is evolving we're pushing changes to this on a daily basis.

Please download and trial for free! We're here to answer any questions about the app or cyber/AI.

story_text.value:
One day while I was sitting working on a personal project I was building using Claude Code I decided to give it a prompt about how I want it to build a function for me that would be directly connected to my database, well did I know that I would be shocked with what actually happened. When I started working on this project of mine, I had decided that I would want to use PostgreSQL purely because I felt that it is the one to use as I did not know a lot about the different databases. Soon after I decided that after doing some research it makes a lot of sense to use MySQL for this project and I discussed this with ChatGPT and I changed my database completely and was working with a MySQL database. To my surprise, the AI models did not realize that, once I got back on Claude and was trying to design a future function something looked not so right to me and there it was - functions were written in a way that I was still using PostgreSQL and they were not at all written in a way for MySQL so it was not possible for them to work and Claude was writing them with so much confidence as in its memory it remembered it as a PostgreSQL.

I was shocked and bamboozled by this honestly so I decided to test it on Cursor and see if it is a thing where the AI model’s memory does not get updated the way it should. That was the moment I decided that I should make Mnemolith, for as insane the name sounds it actually means memory stone and for some reason I thought of carvings on stones as a memory and in this scenario we can change these carvings and basically keep our memory updating. I started building Mnemolith and now I can proudly say that it works on your own local computer (hopefully no bugs but if you find any bugs or anything that I should improve on, please let me know) and is connected to your AI agents like Cursor, Claude Code and Codex. Now memories that are linked to your project files get flagged as soon as those files change, and the user will also find out what happened and they can decide if they want to rewrite what was saved or if it was something that can be ignored. Setup tells the AI models to call Mnemolith, and we let them know which memories changed or were replaced and why, so that they don’t build on old facts and we save time. In our system, each memory stores a hash of the files it depends on so even before a commit we are able to find what changes and the best part is that this all started as a codecrafter’s challenge on building your own redis using java. I would love to know what your AI keeps getting wrong about your projects and any feedback regarding this and things I should work on in the future.

title.value: Show HN: Mnemolith – AI coding memory that goes stale when your code changes
